scope: Conventions that complement docs/reference/PATTERN-STANDARDS-AND-CONVENTIONS.md. Does not duplicate that file; defines notch types, line types, label phrases, regional sizing variants, and block conventions for the major garment families.

notch_types.label: Single notch
notch_types.drawing: one short cut perpendicular to cut edge, ~3-5 mm deep
notch_types.convention: Front pattern pieces and front-side seams. The single notch on a back pattern piece is reserved for side seams that meet a front piece's single notch.
notch_types.use: Identify front-of-garment edges, mark a balance point, indicate seam allowance value when placed at corners
notch_types.machine_inputs_consumed: edge position (distance along seam from a known endpoint)
notch_types.machine_outputs: alignment marker between two paired panels

notch_types.label: Double notch
notch_types.drawing: two parallel short cuts ~3-5 mm apart
notch_types.convention: Back pattern pieces and back-side seams. Differentiates back from front when panels are otherwise mirror-similar.
notch_types.use: Identify back-of-garment edges, especially on sleeve back vs sleeve front
notch_types.machine_outputs: alignment marker between two paired panels

notch_types.label: Triple notch
notch_types.convention: Used sparingly. Sometimes denotes center back on a continuous waistband or sleeve underarm seam to keep orientation unambiguous.
notch_types.use: Disambiguation in patterns with rotational or near-rotational symmetry

notch_types.label: T-notch
notch_types.drawing: T shape: long perpendicular cut into seam allowance with a short cap inside the seam allowance
notch_types.convention: Indicates seam allowance interior limits. Common in industrial patterns where notches are punched not cut. The cap of the T sits at the seam line, the stem at the cut line.
notch_types.use: Marks both the cut edge alignment and the seam line position simultaneously, useful for fold/pleat lines and dart legs
notch_types.machine_outputs: two-point alignment marker (cut edge + seam line)

notch_types.label: Balance mark
notch_types.drawing: context-dependent; typically a single notch placed at a fit-critical alignment point
notch_types.convention: Used to control ease distribution along curves. The most common cases are the sleeve cap front/back balance, princess seam balance at bust apex, and gathered skirt/bodice balance at center and quarter points.
notch_types.use: Distribute ease along curves where two seams of different lengths must be eased into each other
notch_types.machine_inputs_consumed: edge position on each of two paired curves

notch_types.label: Drill hole / circle / dot
notch_types.drawing: small circle or punched hole inside the panel
notch_types.convention: Marks interior reference points: dart apex, pocket placement, button placement, end of slits.
notch_types.use: Interior point markers, not edge markers

line_types.label: Cut line
line_types.role: True boundary along which fabric is cut

line_types.label: Seam line / stitch line
line_types.drawing: dashed line offset inward from cut line by seam allowance
line_types.role: Where stitching occurs; pattern truth for length matching, dart geometry, ease distribution
line_types.geometry_role: inset polygon of panel by seam allowance

line_types.label: Fold line
line_types.drawing: dashed or single-line bracket parallel to fold edge with `cut on fold` text
line_types.role: Edge that is placed on fabric fold, doubling the panel symmetrically
line_types.geometry_role: edge classified as fold-axis; mirror-reflects panel for layout and validation

line_types.label: Grainline
line_types.drawing: long arrow with arrowheads on both ends, parallel to warp direction
line_types.role: Fabric warp direction relative to panel; primary directional convention
line_types.geometry_role: vector orientation of panel for cutting, hang, drape

line_types.label: Dart leg
line_types.drawing: two solid lines meeting at dart apex inside or at panel edge
line_types.role: Boundary of fabric removed by dart fold

line_types.label: Dart apex
line_types.drawing: small circle at the inner end of the dart legs
line_types.role: Endpoint of the dart fold; sewing terminates here
line_types.geometry_role: interior point, vertex of dart triangle

line_types.label: Balance line / horizontal balance
line_types.drawing: thin horizontal line labeled `bust line`, `waist line`, `hip line`
line_types.role: Reference horizontals used for grading, fit checks, validation
line_types.geometry_role: internal reference line, not a sewing feature

line_types.label: Lengthen/shorten line
line_types.drawing: two parallel lines across the panel labeled `lengthen or shorten here`
line_types.geometry_role: internal annotation; geometry-changing operation when applied

line_types.label: Internal feature line
line_types.drawing: thin dashed or marked line for pocket placement, pleat fold, tuck, slit, button placement
line_types.role: Construction-only marking, not a cut or seam

line_types.label: Buttonhole line
line_types.drawing: small horizontal or vertical line with end caps, sized to button diameter + 3mm
line_types.geometry_role: interior annotation with size and orientation

cut_count_phrasing.meaning: Cut once with one panel edge placed on a fabric fold; resulting fabric panel is symmetric across the fold edge.
Cut a single piece, typically asymmetric (e.g. wrap front, single placket).
Cut twice with fabric folded right-sides together OR pattern flipped, producing left/right pair.
Cut twice in identical orientation; produces two identical pieces (e.g. cuffs, pockets).
Cut four; common for collars/cuffs/facings where outer + inner + interfacing pairs are needed.
Cut once in fashion fabric and once in lining.
Cut once in fashion fabric and once in fusible interfacing.

annotation_phrasing_recommendations: Prefer plain language: 'cut on fold', 'right side', 'wrong side', 'place on fold'
Avoid acronyms in user-facing labels (CB, CF, HPS) unless paired with full term in pattern key
When seam allowance varies by edge, label each edge in mm or in directly on the cut line

us.basis: no single legal standard; brand-driven; ASTM D5585 size tables exist for misses figure types
us.notes: Brand sizing varies wildly. Pattern brands (Vogue, McCall's, Big4) typically run 1-2 sizes smaller than RTW.

eu.basis: EU number ≈ bust circumference in cm minus 76 for women; aligned with EN 13402 / ISO 8559
eu.notes: EN 13402 introduced pictograms with bust/hip in cm directly on labels; rarely used at retail.

uk.basis: UK number = US number + 4 conventionally (UK 12 ≈ US 8 ≈ EU 38)
uk.notes: Independent pattern designers in the UK often use UK numeric sizing.

jp.basis: JIS L 4005; size code structure: number-figure_letter-height_letter (e.g. 9-A-R)
jp.notes: Japanese sizes encode three-axis fit (size, drop, stature) directly into the size code.

rough_conversion_notes: JP ≈ US * 0.85 with offset; e.g. US 4 ≈ JP 9 (roughly five Japanese-numeric units higher than US-numeric)
When made-to-measure, prefer ISO 8559 measurement vocabulary internally and present whichever regional code the user expects.

block_sloper_conventions.definition: A block (sloper) is a fitted base pattern with wearing ease only, no design ease, no seam allowance, no closure detail. It is the ground truth from which designs are flat-pattern manipulated.

common_blocks.label: Sleeveless bodice block
common_blocks.notes: Aldrich's sleeveless block: ~2.36 cm ease across bust, ~5.86 cm ease across upper bust/underarm.

common_blocks.label: Trouser block
common_blocks.key_feature: front + back crotch curves; back rise typically 3-5 cm taller than front

common_blocks.label: Fitted (one-piece) sleeve block
common_blocks.key_feature: sleeve cap height and circumference must match armhole within ease ratio (typically 8-15% ease for woven set-in)

common_blocks.label: Torso block (combined bodice + skirt to hip)
common_blocks.key_feature: used for sheath dresses and as base for many one-piece garments without waist seam

common_blocks.label: Knit block (T-shirt sloper)
common_blocks.notes: Drafted with negative ease to account for fabric stretch. Sleeve cap ease minimal (1-2% or zero).

characteristics: explicit ease values stated per zone
torso foundation as starting point for many designs
five-piece basic set: bodice F/B, fitted sleeve, skirt F/B
well documented and widely used in JP industry
tends to produce shorter torso blocks suited to JP body proportions
